issues.problem: The brief treats Corner Tile as if it could reach the court soon. But the 2026-27 City Edition is already designed, approved and in production, and the brief never calls Corner Tile a 2027-28 concept. The calendar doesn't set the NBA approval window for the next set, and the Association set is already white-based.
issues.fix: Label Corner Tile as the 2027-28 City Edition pitch, with a back-planned approval timeline. For 2026-27, put the tile, iron-lace and ward language on lifestyle product that rides the existing City Edition. Pull Glazed White as the base, or define it against the Association white, since NBA rules require the two sets to contrast.

issues.problem: Ward Call launches at a "home opener" whose date is unverified. The Oct 20 opening-night slate doesn't include New Orleans, and the first known Pelicans game is Oct 30 at the Clippers. The pack also needs one paid artist per ward, many school licenses, high-school sign-offs and a Big Freedia booking within about 3 weeks.
issues.fix: Phase it. Launch with 2 or 3 wards and a handful of schools at the first confirmed home game. Roll out the full 17 wards and the school co-brands from December to February. Hold the Freedia set until her footwear and apparel status is cleared, and lead with a bounce lineup of named queer pioneers (Katey Red, Sissy Nobby).

issues.problem: Licensed co-brands with St. Aug, Edna Karr, Warren Easton and McDonogh 35 involve minors, school marks and athletic departments that may be tied to other brands. LHSAA, Orleans Parish and charter-network rules apply too. The brief calls this licensing but names no process.
issues.fix: Start with one willing program or alumni association. Route everything through the school's licensing and athletic office, and make the giveback (gear, gym or team funds) the headline. Treat the school line as a 2027 phase-two item, not an October launch item.

issues.problem: The Bayou Classic band collaboration is built around St. Augustine's Marching 100, a New Orleans high school band. But the Battle of the Bands is between Southern and Grambling. The drop also lands on Nov 27, a Cup Friday, with the Superdome area full of rival-brand HBCU tailgates.
issues.fix: Either center the Bayou Classic piece on HBCU-coded product, using the two universities' own licensing and band programs (and Xavier and Dillard locally). Or keep the St. Aug collaboration as a separate local brass story outside Classic weekend. Check the Pelicans' Nov 27 schedule before planning a pop-up.

issues.problem: One headline artist is carrying the whole bounce story. Bounce credit belongs to a group (Katey Red, Sissy Nobby, DJ Jubilee and others), so a single paid booking risks reading as star-casting. Her footwear and apparel obligations are also unknown.
issues.fix: Pay a rotating roster of bounce artists and DJs for the ward call-and-response. Put the credit on the product and in the arena, and offer the commission to bounce pioneers before the headliner.

issues.target: partners[Dirty Coast, Fleurty Girl] rapid-response tees
issues.problem: The plan has local brands make quick player tees. But player names and numbers fall under NBA and NBPA group licensing, which a local brand can't sublicense, and the brief itself notes the "Who Dat" history. Without those approvals, a pre-cleared program isn't feasible on a turnaround of days.
issues.fix: Make the rapid-response tees city-only, with no player likenesses. Or get Pelicans and NBPA clearance up front for a fixed list of designs and a fixed turn time. Keep the local brands as co-designers of the voice, and pay them as such.

issues.problem: The Twelfth Night Pack leans on purple, green and gold, yet the brief says the Carnival palette is spent and the fan-favorite City Edition already owns it. The King Cake Baby hunt and co-branded cake are fun but thin as a design idea. The food co-brand also has shipping, shelf-life and food-safety limits.
issues.fix: Keep the sanding-sugar texture and the Baby, but cut the palette to a navy ground with a small fleck. Run the cake as an in-arena giveaway, not a bundled retail item. Confirm Pelicans ownership of the King Cake Baby for apparel before building around it.

issues.problem: A Tết x Carnival tee ties a church-centered family holiday to Carnival, with a short window before Mardi Gras Day. Pairing a community's New Year with a Carnival theme risks making it a novelty. The brief also names the Mary Queen of Vietnam gathering in a drop plan.
issues.fix: Move it off the product calendar. Instead, fund or host a community moment: pay Vietnamese New Orleanian artists to design a Pelicans game-night element, or name Dong Phuong as a food partner. Ask the community whether it wants a product at all.

issues.problem: The plan assumes "Cup Friday home nights", a Memphis rivalry graphic and a Cup-colorway capsule. But only the Oct 30 Cup opener (at the Clippers) is known, and the home dates are unconfirmed. There's also no Cup-specific uniform, only the standard sets, so the brief can't promise a Cup colorway.
issues.fix: Tie Cup events to confirmed home dates only, and use a generic Friday-night-in-New-Orleans graphic that works against any Cup opponent. Drop the "Cup colorway" language. Keep the Memphis graphic only if the home date is confirmed.

issues.target: calendar (Oak Street Po-Boy Festival, Red Beans Monday tee)
issues.problem: A hoodie wrapped in butcher paper and a Monday red-beans tee are novelty food references with no clear fan, price or reason to buy. The November hoodie is for a festival that is only a day of walking. Beside the stronger craft ideas, they read like tourist-guide gags.
issues.fix: Fold them into one community gesture: pay Feed the Second Line and the Krewe of Red Beans to design a Monday home-night element. Cut the Po-Boy Festival item.

issues.problem: The club commission is the best idea in the brief. But the plan has Nike underwriting parade permits and police fees, and pushes a release "the week after the parade" as a limited sneaker. Club colors stay secret until parade day. A release that depends on a club's schedule, can't be previewed and needs its sign-off clashes with Nike's lead times. It could also read as buying the culture.
issues.fix: Make the first season a no-product pilot. Pay the club and band, fund the fees through a culture-bearer intermediary, and let the club decide whether and when product exists. Plan a numbered, small-run, club-owned release only if the club asks for one.

issues.problem: The brief gives the museum "veto rights" as an introducer and advisor. But the museum is a small community institution, not a gatekeeper for every club or tribe. The clubs and tribes must consent for themselves.
issues.fix: Treat the museum as one paid advisor and ask it who else should be at the table. Get written consent from each club and band directly. Keep the Black Masking Indian line as "no product, no reference", and don't use Super Sunday or St. Joseph's Night in any plan.

issues.problem: The Claiborne Oaks story turns a documented loss to a Black neighborhood, the overpass that removed the oaks, into a product theme. It's credible only if the artists lead. Putting it on an NBA uniform as an alternate puts a community wound under a swoosh.
issues.fix: Keep it as an artist-owned capsule, with the artists choosing the beneficiary and the credit. Take it off the uniform alternates list. Brief it to Studio BE only as an invitation, with room to decline.

issues.target: topInsights and collection (fleur-de-lis and Code Noir)
issues.problem: The avoid list states the Code Noir fleur-de-lis point as settled fact. The mark's historical use in branding is real, but how the story is told is contested. The Pelicans' own mark also uses the fleur-de-lis, so the brief's stance conflicts with the team's identity.
issues.fix: Say plainly that the fleur-de-lis is avoided mainly because it reads as Saints and as tourist shorthand. Give the history as a secondary reason, and note that the Pelicans mark already carries it.

issues.problem: Lent starts Feb 10, so fish fries and crawfish boil season begin just after Mardi Gras, not in "mid-March". Boil Season is also tied to a Play-In push that a 26-56 team may not have. And it overlaps with Super Sunday and St. Joseph's Night in the same weeks.
issues.fix: Start the Boil Season story in late February or early March, around the team's actual schedule. Keep the Play-In tee as a contingency only. Avoid Super Sunday weekend (Mar 14, 2027) and St. Joseph's Night (Mar 19) entirely.

issues.problem: The hoops and retail dossiers point to Xavier, Dillard, Southern and the HBCU fan base. They also point to LHSAA playoffs, when school pride peaks from February to March. Then there's the Sugar Bowl crowd, and Louisiana-wide Gulf South fans: Baton Rouge, Acadiana, the Gulf Coast. The brief uses none of these as a partner or window.
issues.fix: Add an HBCU capsule with Xavier and Dillard (and Southern and Grambling for Classic). Add a Friday-night school-rivalry home night timed to the LHSAA playoffs. Add a Gulf South regional product line sold outside the metro.

issues.problem: The underground dossier's St. Claude and Marigny layer (Zeitgeist, AllWays Lounge, Hi-Ho), drag and Southern Decadence are barely used. The actual courts (Joe W. Brown Park, Behrman) and the summer heat-led hooper's needs appear only as a heat note in the retail playbook.
issues.fix: Make one court-based event at Joe W. Brown or Behrman, with mesh and sleeveless product. Add a Southern Decadence or Halloween bounce night with the queer artists credited. Pitch both as paid collaborations, not drops.

issues.target: pulse and risks (Zion and Jordan Brand)
issues.problem: Zion is flagged as a Jordan Brand conflict, yet the brief still assigns him "kids swingman" and player tees in the holiday core. It lists the Murphy-first strategy without checking Nike's own relationships with Murphy, Queen and Fears. Player product depends on which of them Nike actually signs.
issues.fix: Confirm each player's apparel arrangement before assigning product. Run Zion pieces through Jordan Brand, and make the Nike-signed names the lead in the holiday plan. If that can't be confirmed, lead with city and ward product in the holiday window.

issues.problem: The brief says "sell the city, not the team" for a team whose product it also needs to move. The 56 opportunity score looks high given retail 34 and fandom 38. The plan also sets a 70% sell-through KPI by Feb 1 for a regional market with a small team-gear base.
issues.fix: Lower the sell-through target and set an expectation per tier (entry tees versus premium). Say how much of the plan is team-branded. Consider an opportunity score nearer the mid-40s.

strengths: The strategy puts the city mark first and the team mark second. It grounds that in real local behavior: phrase tees over team gear, ward and school identity, and the Saints and LSU competing for the same closet.

The Corner Tile concept (tile street names, iron-lace, sign-painter lettering, brass) passes the swap test. It avoids the Carnival palette the fan-favorite City Edition already owns, and keeps Black Masking Indian beadwork and ceremonial imagery out.

The calendar follows the city's own clock: king cake, Mardi Gras Day on Feb 9, 2027, second-line season, Essence, Jazz Fest. It sensibly keeps hero launches out of the two weeks before Carnival and away from Super Sunday and Aug 29.
The pay-and-credit stance is specific: parade fees, instruments through named programs, proceeds to community groups the artists choose, and credit on the product.
Weighting the plan toward city-first product that sells whatever the standings is the right call for a 26-56 team with a new coach and a thin retail base.
summary: The brief is strong on culture and specificity, with a design language no other city could wear and a careful line on sacred material. Delivery is weaker. Corner Tile can't be the 2026-27 uniform, Ward Call is overloaded for an October launch, and NBA and NBPA licensing blocks the rapid-response tee. Fix the sequencing, let the communities set the terms, and cut the novelty items.
